# Defender — World Model Network Attack Forecasting System

> Problem Statement ID: 26153  
> Organization: National Technical Research Organisation (NTRO)  
> Title: AI based Network Attack Forecasting from Network Traffic Data  
> Core Paradigm: Predictive Cyber Defence via Learned State Dynamics P(S_{t+1} | S_t)

## Executive Summary
Defender is an offline-first AI system developed for NTRO Problem Statement 26153. Traditional intrusion detection evaluates network flows in isolation using static binary classification. In contrast, Defender implements a **Network World Model** that learns an internal causal simulation of how network states evolve over time windows. 

Given observed traffic state $S_t$, the world model predicts the probability distribution over future states $P(S_{t+1} \vert S_t)$, enabling forward simulation $K$ steps ahead to forecast attack trajectories before compromise is completed.

## Dual-Level Traffic Feature Pipeline
The system ingests both flow-level and packet-level features drawn from open-source network traffic datasets:

### 1. Flow-Level Features (NetFlow / IPFIX)
- Source and Destination IP / Port pairs
- TCP Flag bitmask: SYN, ACK, FIN, RST, PSH, URG
- Protocol Number
- Bytes transferred per flow & Packets per flow
- Flow duration (ms)
- Inter-Arrival Time (IAT) statistics: Mean, Variance, Max
- Bidirectional flow ratios

### 2. Packet-Level Features (PCAP-Derived)
- Time-To-Live (TTL) mean & variance across sessions
- TCP window size distributions
- IP fragment flags
- Payload size distributions
- Port scan signatures (sequential vs. randomized access entropy)
- Retransmission counts

## World Model Architecture
- **State Representation**: Continuous feature vectors $S_t$ or graph representations encoding active traffic flows in time window $t$.
- **Sequence Models**: LSTM, Temporal Transformer, and Graph Neural Networks (GNN) trained on ground-truth state transition sequences.
- **K-Step Forward Simulation**: Projects infiltration likelihood across future horizons ($K = 1 \dots 10$).
- **MITRE ATT&CK Mapping**: Maps forecasted future states to kill-chain tactics:
  - Reconnaissance (TA0043)
  - Initial Access (TA0001)
  - Lateral Movement (TA0008)
  - Command & Control (TA0011)
  - Exfiltration (TA0010)

## Explainability & Decision Support
- **SHAP Feature Attribution**: Quantifies exact marginal contribution of individual flags, timing statistics, and port access patterns to the forecasted risk score.
- **Temporal Attention Distributions**: Exposes which prior time windows informed the current state transition.

## Supported Datasets & Benchmarks
- **CSE-CIC-IDS2018**: Cross-day evaluation (Wednesday train, Thursday held-out test).
- **CTU-13**: Real-world botnet scenarios with ground-truth temporal labels.
- **UNSW-NB15**: Multi-stage attack flows.
- **CICIoT2023**: IoT protocol telemetry.
- **Raw .pcap**: Direct ingestion via Scapy / PyShark offline parsing.
- **Baseline Comparison**: Empirically validated against Logistic Regression baseline demonstrating superior F1 score and reduced False Positive Rate (FPR).
